This lecture covers four ideas that keep a database reliable, efficient and secure. Normalization splits large tables into smaller related ones to reduce duplication and the insertion, update and deletion anomalies, through the normal forms 1NF, 2NF, 3NF and BCNF. A transaction is a group of operations treated as one unit of work, as in a bank transfer; its ACID properties (atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability) keep the results correct. Concurrency control, for example locking and timestamp ordering, manages many users at the same time, and logs and checkpoints support recovery after a failure. Finally, authentication and authorization, strong passwords, appropriate permissions, encryption, backups and monitoring protect data from unauthorized access, modification or destruction.
